title: Thou God of Hope, to Thee We Bow
description: Thou God of Hope, to Thee We Bow in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 782 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Care of Widows and Orphans”, where the book credits them to the Ch. Psalmody.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thou God of hope, to thee we bow; Thou art our re-fuge in dis-tress; The hus-band of the wid-ow thou, The fa-ther of the fa-ther-less.

lines: Thou God of hope, to thee we bow;
Thou art our refuge in distress;
The husband of the widow thou,
The poor are thy peculiar care;
To them thy promises are sure:
Thy gifts the poor in spirit share;
O, may we always thus be poor.
May we thy law of love fulfil,
To bear each other's burdens here,
Endure and do thy righteous will,
And walk in all thy faith and fear.
Thou God of hope, to thee we bow;
Thou art our refuge in distress;
The husband of the widow thou,
